answer: Sybil resistance makes coordinated equivocation costly: when k identities share correlated evidence, pairwise attribution causes penalties to scale as O(k²), rather than linearly with the swarm. Bonded collateral in a vault is slashed on detection, with asymmetric depreciation applying an exponential multiplier to aggregate capital loss. Thus, adding identities can widen the terrace of apparent influence, but detection turns that strategy into a steep spiral of liability.
